title: Continuity and evaluation scalar comparison under internal-to-section module equivalence
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme with small pro-étale site in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\Lambda,\Gamma$ be commutative condensed rings and $a:\Lambda\to\Gamma$ a ring-object map [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Put $R=p_X^*\Lambda$, $S=p_X^*\Gamma$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and write $a_X:R\to S$ and $a_{\rm sec}:R_{\rm sec}\to S_{\rm sec}$ for its internal and reconstructed section-ring maps [def-sfb-section-scalar-map-data]. Assume ordinary internal extension of scalars along $a_Z$ is exact for every scheme $Z$ [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Use ordinary unbounded module derived categories, relative K-flat tensor and ambient internal Hom $H_R^{\rm int},H_S^{\rm int}$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], and the ringed-site K-flat tensor and K-injective Hom $H_{R_{\rm sec}},H_{S_{\rm sec}}$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $F_B$ be the equivalence from internal $B$-modules to section-ring module sheaves, preserving underlying abelian sheaves and maps, and put $\Phi_B=D(F_B)$ for $B=R,S$ [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence].

The normalized internal-to-sectionwise derived tensor comparisons [def-sfb-internal-section-derived-tensor-comparison] and the evaluation-normalized Hom identifications
$$\Phi_B H_B^{\rm int}(K,N)\simeq H_{B_{\rm sec}}(\Phi_BK,\Phi_BN)$$
identify the following maps and conditions. For every small filtered diagram $(M_i^\bullet)$ of internal $R$-module complexes with a common termwise lower bound, the evaluation-induced map
$$\varinjlim_i H_R^{\rm int}(K,M_i^\bullet)\longrightarrow H_R^{\rm int}(K,\varinjlim_iM_i^\bullet)$$
is carried to the corresponding map for $\Phi_RK$ and $(F_RM_i^\bullet)$; here both sides use exact termwise sheaf colimits of transported functorial representatives [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Thus continuity for every such diagram is equivalent in the two presentations. The functors $F_B$ preserve the common termwise bound, and $\Phi_B$ preserves and reflects every cohomological lower bound.

Write $A^{\rm int}=S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ and $A^{\rm sec}=S_{\rm sec}\otimes_{R_{\rm sec}}^{\mathbf L}-$ (K-flat derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]), with their scalar-unit normalized tensor comparisons [def-sfb-internal-scalar-tensor-comparison]. Under the canonical scalar-extension and restriction identifications $\Phi_S A^{\rm int}\simeq A^{\rm sec}\Phi_R$, the evaluation-transpose map
$$c^{\rm int}_{K,L}:A^{\rm int}H_R^{\rm int}(K,L)\longrightarrow H_S^{\rm int}(A^{\rm int}K,A^{\rm int}L)$$
is carried by $\Phi_S$ to $c^{\rm sec}_{\Phi_RK,\Phi_RL}$. This equality is natural in both inputs and compatible with composable exact coefficient maps. It identifies the restricted comparisons under the evaluation-normalized scalar adjunction, and, for every small filtered diagram of these exact coefficient maps, the evaluation maps at its objects, the squares for its arrows and the induced maps on termwise filtered colimits. Finite freeness and algebra/module colimit cocones with specified maps are unchanged by section reconstruction. No boundedness or continuity assumption is needed for this comparison of maps; the continuity equivalence above applies to arbitrary $K$.

proof.text: For $B=R,S$, [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] makes $F_B$ exact and identifies the regular module, ordinary tensors and total tensor complexes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to obtain $H^n(F_BC)=F_BH^n(C)$. An equivalence reflects zero objects: if $F_BM=0$, apply its inverse. Hence $\Phi_BC$ has zero cohomology in every degree below $b$ exactly when $C$ does. At the complex level $F_B0=0$, so a common termwise lower bound is preserved by $F_B$ and its inverse. Neither conclusion needs a bound on $K$ or on its internal Hom.

proof.text: Reconstruction transports every small module cocone, with its legs: given a cocone out of $(F_BM_i)$, apply the inverse equivalence, use the original colimit universal property, and apply $F_B$ back; the two constructions are inverse on the unique mediating map. Apply this degreewise to complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], module colimits have the underlying abelian sheaf colimit, and that forgetful functor is faithful and exact. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact] gives exact small filtered colimits of module sheaves; transport gives the same assertion internally. In particular, these termwise filtered colimits preserve quasi-isomorphisms, since exactness commutes with the kernels and images defining cohomology. This justifies the representative convention in the statement; it does not identify arbitrary underived colimits in a derived category.

Apply [lem-sfb-module-object-ringed-site-derived-comparison] separately for $R$ and $S$. Its hypotheses are precisely the small-site, pulled-back condensed coefficient and ordinary K-flat tensor conventions in the statement. Write $\theta_B:\Phi_BH_B^{\rm int}(C,D)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{B_{\rm sec}}(\Phi_BC,\Phi_BD)$ for its natural isomorphism. Its evaluation equation says that $\theta_B$, together with the fixed normalized tensor comparison, carries internal evaluation to sectionwise evaluation. Consequently a morphism into either Hom object corresponds to its transported morphism into the other exactly when their tensor-Hom transposes correspond: apply the adjunction bijection to the evaluation equation. The same holds with evaluation on the other side of the tensor by the symmetry compatibility of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison].

proof.text: Let $M=\varinjlim_iM_i$ and let $u_i:M_i\to M$ be its actual termwise cocone. Naturality of $\theta_R$ gives, for each leg, $\theta_{R,K,M}\,\Phi_R(H_R^{\rm int}(K,u_i))=H_{R_{\rm sec}}(\Phi_RK,F_Ru_i)\,\theta_{R,K,M_i}$. These are the evaluation-induced leg maps by step 3. Choose the functorial Hom representatives on the section side and transport the entire functorial system, including the maps to the representative at $M$, through $F_R^{-1}$, as stipulated in the statement. On these representatives $F_R$ carries each chain leg to that very same sectionwise leg. Step 2 therefore carries the chain map induced from their termwise colimit to the same chain map on the section side: both have the specified leg composites, so uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] applies degreewise. Localizing gives the asserted equality of continuity maps, not just an isomorphism of their sources and targets. An equivalence preserves and reflects isomorphisms, and every section-side diagram with a common bound transports back with that bound by step 1. This proves continuity equivalence for arbitrary $K$. In the Lean representative formulation, continuity_map_transport is proved directly by precomposing with every transported colimit leg and using naturality of homRepresentativeIso. For continuity_iff, apply preservation and reflection of quasi-isomorphisms by the exact equivalence to the isomorphism of arrows just proved. Every section diagram is isomorphic to the image of its inverse-equivalence transport. The termwise lower-bound equivalence transports the bound back, so quantification over all such diagrams agrees in both directions. This comparison of representative arrows needs no exact-filtered-colimit argument beyond the existing representative conventions.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction] for $a_X$ to obtain $\alpha:\Phi_SA^{\rm int}\xrightarrow{\sim}A^{\rm sec}\Phi_R$ and the restriction square, identifying the specified units and counits. These comparisons also identify the strong tensor maps: before derivation both routes take $s\otimes(m\otimes n)$ to $(s\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)$. The internal formula is [def-sfb-internal-scalar-tensor-comparison]; the section formula is [lem-sfb-scalar-ordinary-tensor-comparison], and the intermediate presentation comparisons fix pure tensors by [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. Equality on balanced generators is equality of morphisms by the tensor universal property. On a pair of flat-term K-flat representatives this same equality holds on each total summand, hence on the total complex and its localization. These compute both derived maps by the normalized representative squares in [def-sfb-internal-section-derived-tensor-comparison] and, on the section side, the full K-flat representative square of the scalar tensor comparison in [def-sfb-scalar-hom-comparison-data]. Thus the scalar tensor square agrees for arbitrary derived inputs. The assumed exactness on every scheme supplies the exactness hypothesis of the internal scalar normalization; since $F_R,F_S$ are exact equivalences, $\alpha$ shows that ordinary sheafified extension along $a_{\rm sec}$ is exact too, which is the hypothesis of [lem-sfb-hom-flat-scalar-evaluation-model] used in steps 6–9; it is not an assertion that an arbitrary Hom complex is K-flat.

For either presentation write $e_R:H_R(K,L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\to L$ for right evaluation and $\mu$ for the scalar comonoidal map. By definition the closed transpose of $c_{K,L}$ is
$$A H_R(K,L)\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}AK\xrightarrow{\mu^{-1}}A(H_R(K,L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K)\xrightarrow{A(e_R)}AL.$$
Conjugate the internal map by $\alpha$ and $\theta_R,\theta_S$. Step 5 identifies the first arrow with $(\mu^{\rm sec})^{-1}$, and step 3 identifies $e_R$ with sectionwise evaluation; naturality of $\alpha$ identifies $A(e_R)$ with $A^{\rm sec}(e_{R_{\rm sec}})$. The conjugated map consequently has exactly the displayed sectionwise transpose. Injectivity of the closed adjunction bijection proves that it is $c^{\rm sec}_{\Phi_RK,\Phi_RL}$. This calculation uses actual maps throughout; it neither assumes the comparison is invertible nor any boundedness or continuity.

proof.text: Naturality of the equality in step 6 follows from naturality of $\alpha,\theta$ and the sectionwise comparison, the latter for arbitrary derived morphisms by [lem-sfb-hom-flat-scalar-evaluation-model]. For composable exact coefficient maps, the ordinary scalar compositors in the two presentations send $t\otimes(s\otimes m)$ to $t\,b(s)\otimes m$ and identify the scalar units. Thus their two possible presentation comparisons agree by the extension/restriction adjunction of [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction]; localize on K-flat representatives for the derived compositors. The sectionwise identity and composition equations for $c$ are exactly the equations of [lem-sfb-hom-flat-scalar-evaluation-model]. Substitute the equality of step 6 for each of the three coefficient maps in that composition equation and cancel the presentation isomorphisms. Faithfulness of $\Phi$ gives the internal equation and shows that its transport is the specified sectionwise equation. This includes identity coefficient maps.

proof.text: Consider the restriction identification $U H_S(AK,N)\cong H_R(K,UN)$. Its five Hom bijections and its determining equation (restricted evaluation after the scalar unit) are [lem-sfb-closed-scalar-hom-comparison]; on the section side this is exactly [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction]. Steps 3 and 5 identify every closed transpose, scalar transpose, unit and tensor map in this string. The transported internal identification therefore equals the sectionwise identification by the uniqueness in that determining equation. Apply this with $N=AL$ and compose with $U(c_{K,L})$. Step 6 and the restriction square identify that composite, giving the claimed equality of the restricted comparisons with their evaluation normalization.

proof.text: For a small filtered coefficient diagram, apply steps 5–8 at every object. For an arrow of the diagram, its transition square is the composition equation of step 7, with the fixed restriction identifications of step 8; hence both paths are identified, including their units and evaluations. Transport the whole functorial representative diagram and its cocone, not a collection of separately chosen representatives. As in step 4, $F$ then identifies every chain arrow and leg; the degreewise universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] identifies the induced maps on their termwise filtered colimits. Step 2 supplies exactness when passing quasi-isomorphisms to these colimits. This is a comparison of the induced maps, not a claim that Hom commutes with the colimit. Its invertibility, when required, is precisely the separate continuity condition already compared in step 4. In the Lean coefficient_diagram_evaluation_transport clause, the object normalization is ScalarTransport.hom, the coefficient triangle is Under.w, and the arrow composition equation is internalScalarHom_composition. Transported representative squares follow by applying complexForward.map to f.naturality; naturality of preservesColimitNatIso gives the colimit-map equation.

proof.text: Finally, the ordinary equivalence preserves finite sums and the regular module by [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. Thus an isomorphism $B^n\cong M$ is carried to, and recovered from, $(B_{\rm sec})^n\cong F_BM$, including $n=0$; the same test after restriction treats local finite freeness if used. Module cocones are unchanged by step 2. For algebra cocones, [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf] reconstructs multiplication and unit uniquely from the section operations, while [def-sfb-section-scalar-map-data] leaves the section maps of each ring map unchanged. A map is multiplicative, unital and over the base ring on one side exactly when it is on the other: these are the same equations on sections, or equivalently on the sheaf-tensor coprojections. Hence reconstruction and its inverse give inverse bijections on compatible algebra cocones with any vertex. The existence and uniqueness of each mediator, and its equations with the specified legs, are consequently unchanged. This proves the final cocone and finite-freeness assertions without choosing new transition maps or bases.
